title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: In the text line the map restricted to B̃' is written with subscript G ('σ_G | B̃' : B̃' → S''). It must be σ_{G'}, as in diagram (51); this is a slip of the pen.

The universal-property sentence reads 'morphismes généralisés de G dans un graphe G''. Mathematically it should be generalized morphisms from G' to an arbitrary graph that send the arcs of C̃' to identities. The insertion is a slip or a transcription artefact.
Minor gap: connectedness of the fibres is used to get π_0(G'_•) ≅ S. The pushout statement itself holds without it, as the next page notes, but then S must be defined as π_0(G'_•) rather than given.

ideas.what: Graphs as (vertices, half-edges with fixed-point-free involution, incidence map), with generalized morphisms allowing edges to collapse to vertices
ideas.modern_name: Flag/half-edge formalism for graphs; category of (stable) graphs with contractions
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{g,ν} and the Teichmüller tower but not this formalism explicitly

ideas.what: Reconstruction of the contracted graph from (G', set of surviving edges B')
Contraction as a pushout G' ⊔_{G'_•} π_0(G'_•) in the category of graphs with generalized morphisms, with its universal property
ideas.modern_name: Contraction as cocartesian square / universal edge collapse
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; made explicit in operadic graph categories (e.g. Borisov–Manin; Joyal–Kock style graph categories)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine formalization of edge contraction for dual graphs of stable curves. It anticipates the half-edge and contraction formalism later standard in modular operad theory. Nothing on this page is mathematically new or likely to surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: the map is written σ (or ∂) with subscript G restricted to B̃'. The intended subscript is G', consistent with diagram (51).
Under diagram (52), 'ponctuel' is struck out and replaced by 'discret': 'graphe discret défini par S =déf π_0(G'_•)'.
In (52) the lower-left object appears as 'S = π_0(G'_•)', with a heavily overwritten letter, possibly S'_• corrected to G'_•.
Universal property line: the inserted words above 'graphes' read roughly 'G dans un', but the sense requires generalized morphisms from G' into a graph.
